clue.text: It describes the nature of work, as in "Plans work out"

definitions.text: It describes the nature of work

indicators.note: work out here means be worked into a new shape, so the quoted letters and 'as in' are rearranged

explanation.surface: A management maxim is illustrated by a sample saying about how plans pan out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the thirteen letters of AS IN plus PLANS WORK. The quotation marks make 'Plans work out' look like the example, but the words are only the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous 1955 maxim of C. Northcote Parkinson says work expands to fill the time available for its completion.

clue.text: Distressed, I feared Gestapo might discover food

indicators.note: distressed means upset and disordered, telling us to rearrange the letters

explanation.surface: Someone frightened that the secret police might find something to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Distressed' rearranges the fourteen letters of I FEARED GESTAPO.
explanation.definitionFit: Pâté de foie gras is a rich French delicacy made from fattened goose or duck liver.

clue.text: Like 13, with a lot of grass

definitions.meaning: resembling the tone of the woodwind instrument at 13, thin and nasal
full of tall waterside grasses such as rushes

explanation.definitionFit: A double-reed instrument has a thin piping tone, and a marshy bank full of tall rushes is thick with reeds.

clue.text: No longer suspected, I can let her out

indicators.note: out means the letters are let out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone cleared of suspicion is allowed to be released.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges I CAN LET HER.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in the clear is to be free of suspicion or blame.

clue.text: West Midlands town featured in a Bronte novel

definitions.meaning: a suburban town near Solihull in the English West Midlands
the 1849 novel by Charlotte Brontë named after its heroine

explanation.definitionFit: Shirley is a suburb of Solihull in the West Midlands county of England, and Charlotte Brontë's second published novel takes its title from its heroine.

clue.text: Budding climber makes it, proceeding from foot of Matterhorn

indicators.note: proceeding from means the climb follows on from the letter at the bottom of the mountain
the foot of a word in a down clue is its last letter

parts.note: what a climber makes is an ascent, the act of going up

explanation.surface: A novice mountaineer succeeds, setting off from the base of a famous Alpine peak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foot of Matterhorn' is N, the last letter of the word; 'proceeding from' puts ASCENT (what a climber makes) after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Nascent means just coming into being, emerging and starting to develop.

clue.text: Tibetan monk — a native of S. America, they say

indicators.note: they say means the word is spoken, so we want something that sounds the same

parts.note: the llama is a woolly pack animal native to the Andes

explanation.surface: A Himalayan holy man is said to come from South America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'they say' signals a sound-alike: LLAMA, the Andean animal, is pronounced the same as the Buddhist monk.
explanation.definitionFit: A lama is a Buddhist spiritual teacher or monk in Tibet.

clue.text: Women's waste receptacle when inside, it's used for cleaning

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for women, as on lavatory doors

indicators.note: inside tells us the word for when sits within the receptacle

parts.note: an ash bin is a dustbin, a receptacle for rubbish
as can mean when, as in 'as the sun set'

explanation.surface: A ladies' room bin is cleaned out once it's been put inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' is the container signal; 'when' can mean 'as', and W is the usual sign on a women's lavatory door. The surface pictures a ladies' room bin.
explanation.definitionFit: A washbasin is a sink for washing one's hands and face.

clue.text: Quotes from card "Is Movement Changing?"

indicators.note: changing means altering the order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Lines lifted from a greeting card ask whether a political cause is evolving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changing' rearranges CARD with IS MOVEMENT. 'Quotes' is a noun, the punctuation marks.
explanation.definitionFit: Inverted commas are the punctuation marks used to enclose a quotation.

clue.text: Camp that overlaps Viking's

indicators.note: the two words are made to overlap, like links of a chain, so part of the first slides inside the second

parts.note: taken as written
Eric the Red is the stock crossword Viking, so Viking's gives the name with its S

explanation.surface: A remark that some showy behaviour exceeds even a Norseman's.
explanation.walkthrough: THAT and ERICS overlap: the AT of THAT slips past the E of ERICS, giving TH-E-AT-RICS. ERIC the Red is the usual crossword Viking.
explanation.definitionFit: Camp as a noun is exaggerated, showy behaviour, which is what histrionic theatrics amount to.

clue.text: A society chap — thus an insider

definitions.text: A society chap — thus an insider

indicators.note: the word for 'thus' is said to be an insider, placed within the word for chap

parts.note: a chap is a man
thus means so

explanation.surface: A clubbable fellow is described as one on the inside of things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'an insider' is the container signal. The whole clue is also the definition: a Freemason belongs to a secret society and is very much an insider in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A Freemason is a member of a secretive fraternal society, hence a society man who is on the inside.

clue.text: Do see about author

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the bishop's see is written backwards

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city and bishop's see in Cambridgeshire, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: An instruction to look into something concerning a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the reversal signal. A 'see' is a bishop's seat, and the cathedral city of Ely in Cambridgeshire is the setter's favourite one.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Arthur Conan Doyle was the writer who created Sherlock Holmes.

clue.text: Song told a story

definitions.meaning: a German art song for voice and piano, as by Schubert

explanation.definitionFit: A Lied is a German art song, and someone who fibbed or invented a falsehood has done this.

clue.text: Tramps to be deprived of cover? It's in the wind

indicators.note: losing its cover means the word loses its outside, its first and last letters

parts.note: hoboes are tramps, homeless wanderers

explanation.surface: Vagrants face losing their shelter in the open, exposed to the wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be deprived of cover' strips the first and last letters, H and S, from HOBOES. 'the wind' is the woodwind section, not the weather.
explanation.definitionFit: This double-reed instrument belongs to the woodwind section of an orchestra.

clue.text: Nick and Thomas worked together to make a coat

indicators.note: worked means shaped or kneaded, so the two names are combined and reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: Two tailors collaborate to produce an overcoat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worked together' rearranges NICK and THOMAS as one pool of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A mackintosh is a raincoat, originally made of rubberised cloth.

clue.text: University department's conferred power

definitions.meaning: a division of a university, such as the arts division
an authority or power granted to someone, as in the legal sense

explanation.definitionFit: A university is divided into faculties, and in law a faculty is a licence or authorisation granted by an authority.

clue.text: Dear John won't make a travelling hawker

parts.note: with 'won't' turning it round, what is not dear is inexpensive
Jack is the familiar form of the name John

explanation.surface: A break-up letter will not produce a pedlar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dear John' looks like a jilting letter, but 'won't make' negates 'Dear': not dear is CHEAP; JACK is the pet form of John.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheapjack was an itinerant seller of cheap goods at fairs and markets.

clue.text: Sort of verb I've deleted in this passage

indicators.note: deleted tells us the letters for I've are struck out of the longer word

parts.note: a verb that takes a direct object is the transitive kind
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A grammar note about a verb form removed from this stretch of text.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deleted' removes IVE from TRANSITIVE. 'passage' looks like a stretch of text, which the surface encourages, but it means a journey across.
explanation.definitionFit: Transit is the act of passing through or across, a journey or crossing.

clue.text: To go over it takes an age, ends in utmost fatigue

parts.note: taken as written
an era is an age, a long period of time

indicators.note: ends in points to the closing letter of each of the two following words

explanation.surface: Revising something takes ages and leaves one utterly exhausted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' joins IT to ERA (an age); 'ends in' gives the last letters of 'utmost' and 'fatigue', T and E.
explanation.definitionFit: To iterate is to repeat or say again, which is to go over something once more.

clue.text: Prohibition threw up nothing to attract my interest

indicators.note: in a down clue threw up means the whole string is read from the bottom upward

parts.note: the letter O looks like zero, nothing
to grab me is to attract my interest

explanation.surface: A ban produced nothing to engage me.
explanation.walkthrough: 'threw up' reverses O GRAB ME as one run, which in a down entry reads upward.
explanation.definitionFit: An embargo is an official ban, especially on trade with a country.

clue.text: Roused a man, without being married

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the married word goes round the rest

parts.note: being married means wed
Ken is a man's name

explanation.surface: Someone stirred up a fellow despite not being his spouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, the container signal; the surface reads it as 'lacking'.
explanation.definitionFit: Wakened means stirred from sleep, so roused is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Persuade the French to support western note

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece supports another by sitting under it

parts.note: to note is to pay attention, to heed
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Encouragement for French readers to back a western memo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to support' puts LE (French for 'the') under W and HEED in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To wheedle is to coax or flatter someone into doing something.

clue.text: Opening in State education for a sportsman

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia
PE, physical education, is the schooling a sportsman gets in the gym

explanation.surface: A chance for an athlete to get schooling at a public institution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' is a US state, Georgia, abbreviated GA; PE is physical education, the school sports lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: A gape is a wide opening, as of a beak or a gap.

clue.text: Church not completed by French cleric

indicators.note: something not completed is missing its end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: an abbey is a church, especially one attached to a monastery

explanation.surface: A church left unfinished by a French priest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not completed' cuts the last letter from ABBEY.
explanation.definitionFit: Abbé is the French title for a priest or clergyman.

clue.text: Emperor besieging Germany's capital — a colourful man

indicators.note: besieging means surrounding, so the emperor goes round the letter

parts.note: Nero was the Roman emperor who supposedly fiddled while Rome burned

indicators.note: capital means the first letter of the word Germany

explanation.surface: A Roman emperor lays siege to the German capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'besieging' puts G, the capital of 'Germany's', inside NERO. The answer is a dated term, now offensive; 'colourful' plays on the old word 'coloured'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an old-fashioned, now offensive, term for a Black person, which the setter hints at with a play on the dated word coloured.

clue.text: Wolf — a man short of energy

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so the letter for energy is taken away

parts.note: George is a man's name
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A predator is a fellow running low on vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short of' removes E from GEORGE. 'Wolf' is a verb, to eat greedily.
explanation.definitionFit: To wolf food is to bolt it down greedily, just as one might stuff oneself.

clue.text: A group of countries stop talking

indicators.note: talking means the word is heard spoken, so we want a word that sounds the same

parts.note: to block is to stop or obstruct

explanation.surface: A set of nations halts negotiations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'talking' signals a sound-alike: BLOCK (stop) sounds the same as the political group.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloc is an alliance of nations with shared interests, such as the old Soviet bloc.

clue.text: Girl with one left boot

parts.note: Ava is a girl's name
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A girl and someone else, left with a single boot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boot' is a verb here, in the old sense 'be of use', as in 'what boots it?'; the surface makes it footwear.
explanation.definitionFit: To boot in the archaic sense is to profit or be of use, the same as to be of service.

clue.text: Craft in mid-air sent back not one message

indicators.note: sent back means the assembled letters are read from right to left
in places the vessel within the other word
not one means a letter I is removed from the word mid-air

parts.note: taken as written, without the hyphen
the Roman numeral for one is I
the Argo was the ship of Jason and the Argonauts

explanation.surface: An aircraft high up returned a message, but not a single one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes a letter, 'in' is the container signal and 'sent back' reverses everything, giving the backwards run MARGOIDAR. The Argo was Jason's ship, so 'Craft' is a vessel, not a skill.
explanation.definitionFit: A radiogram is a telegram or other message sent by radio.

clue.text: Those following one closely may be kept waiting

definitions.text: Those following one closely may be kept waiting

parts.words: Those following one closely may be kept waiting
parts.note: people walking right behind someone might literally strike that person's feet, and the phrase also means to be left idly waiting

explanation.surface: Pursuers tailing someone might find themselves made to hang around.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to wait idly or impatiently, while those following close behind could literally knock the walker's feet.
